h: Dawley, the Gorge and the Wrekin
p: Dawley is one of the old industrial towns that were stitched together to make Telford, and it has a cracking claim to fame. It was the birthplace of Captain Matthew Webb, who in 1875 became the first person recorded to swim the English Channel without help. There's a memorial to him in the town, and it's a good story to tell young swimmers.

From the zoo you're only a short drive from the Ironbridge Gorge, a World Heritage Site often called the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution. The Iron Bridge itself, the first major bridge made of cast iron, has crossed the Severn since 1779 and is free to walk over. The Gorge museums are a big day out on their own: Blists Hill Victorian Town recreates a working Victorian street with shops, a bank and costumed characters, while Enginuity lets children try hands-on science and engineering challenges.

For fresh air, the Wrekin, Shropshire's famous lone hill, rises just to the west of Telford. The climb is steep but short enough for older kids, and the views from the top stretch across several counties.

Practical tips: the zoo is ideal for an hour or two, so it suits a morning before heading to Ironbridge. Telford Town Park has big play areas and lakes if the kids need to run about, and plenty of parking makes the whole area easy by car.
